panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (Left, Right). Left: Autopsy external photograph of a 19-week fetus from a case report titled 'Sirenomelia Sympus Dipus', captioned as showing complete lower-limb fusion with a single fused lower extremity and two distal feet — the classic mermaid appearance of sirenomelia. Findings map directly to the configured vocabulary; skin tone is not assessable in a second-trimester macerated fetal specimen. [raw subtype: sympus dipus (Type I)] Right: Anteroposterior fetal radiograph from the same sirenomelia sympus dipus case report, showing an intact cranium, spine and rib cage with absent sacrum/pelvic bones and two femora, two tibiae and two feet within the fused lower extremity, corroborating the Type I (sympus dipus) classification. The fused long bones are not osseously fused, so the 'fused tibial/femoral bones' vocabulary term is not applied; the separate duplicated bones within a fused limb are proposed instead. [raw subtype: sympus dipus (Type I)]

panels.figure_caption: Gross and radiographic findings of sirenomelia sympus dipus in a 19-week male fetus. Left: lateral external gross photograph of the 19-week male fetus demonstrating complete lower-limb fusion (sirenomelia), with both hands positioned at the face, preserved upper extremities, and the characteristic single fused lower extremity with visible feet at the distal end. Right: full anteroposterior fetal radiograph showing an intact cranium, vertebral column, and rib cage; absent sacrum and pelvic bones; and two femora, two tibiae, and two feet within the fused lower extremity — confirming Type I sirenomelia (sympus dipus).
in_text_mentions: Plain radiographs confirmed agenesis of the sacrum and pelvic bones. Two femora, two tibiae, and two feet were identified within the fused lower extremity, corroborating the sympus dipus classification (Figure 2). Placental examination revealed a two-vessel umbilical cord consisting of a single artery and a single vein, with a second-trimester placenta otherwise within normal limits on macroscopic examination.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a neonate with sirenomelia, showing fused lower limbs and absent external genitalia as described in the caption and text.
panels.attribution_text: Al Yaqoubi et al. A Case of Sirenomelia Associated with Hypoplastic Left Heart with a Healthy Co-Twin: A Rare Entity.. Case reports in pediatrics 2018. doi:10.1155/2018/9361745. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Sirenomelic baby showing no genitalia.
in_text_mentions: The neonate was born with severe growth restriction with a weight of 1300 gm and cyanosed with a poor Apgar score. As a result, soon after the delivery, it was shifted to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). Physical examination of the baby revealed microcephaly (head circumference 29 cm), low-set ears, right hand with polysyndactyly, and complete fusion of the entire lower extremities with an absence of feet (Figures 1 and 2). There was no anal opening, and no external genital organs could be identified. The infant was clinically diagnosed as a case of sirenomelia.
